takeaway: A varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus. It may be idiopathic or secondary; exclude abdominal or pelvic malignancy in a new unilateral varicocele.

lines.text: A man develops a scrotal swelling after an open inguinal hernia repair.

lines.say: His G P diagnoses a varicocele.

lines.text: A varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus within the scrotum.
So damage to the pampiniform plexus of veins accounts for it.
It may be idiopathic, from a valve problem in the plexus, or secondary to compression of the testicular venous drainage.
Patients describe a dragging discomfort, or heaviness, in the scrotum.
lines.say: (sigh) Patients describe a dragging discomfort, or heaviness, in the scrotum.

lines.text: And with a new one-sided varicocele, always exclude an abdominal or pelvic malignancy.
